issues.legal_issue: A usufructuary mortgage that identifies land without expressly including cultivatory rights, while the mortgagors continue cultivating it, does not transfer those cultivatory rights to the mortgagees.
material_facts: The mortgage deeds described the land as including sir land but did not expressly include its cultivatory rights.
The mortgagors continued to cultivate the land after the mortgages, and the mortgagees did not take possession for cultivation.
The claim for possession was based on the mortgages.
issues.conclusion: The mortgagees acquired proprietary rights in the land under the mortgages but not the cultivatory rights; the mortgagors became occupancy tenants by the time the 1920 Act came into force.
issues.legal_principle: The court interpreted the mortgage deeds as transferring proprietary rights only where they referred to sir land without expressly transferring cultivatory rights. Because cultivation and actual cultivatory possession remained with the mortgagors, they became ex-proprietary occupancy tenants or, alternatively, tenants who had become occupancy tenants under section 10 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act, 1920. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.possession_claim_based_on_mortgage: A party seeks possession in a suit on the basis of rights said to arise from a mortgage.
predicates.mortgage_only_described_land: The mortgage identified the land but did not expressly include the cultivatory rights in it.
predicates.mortgagors_kept_cultivation: The mortgagors continued cultivating the land, and the mortgagees did not take possession for cultivation.

issues.definition: When a possession claim rests on a mortgage that only describes the land and the mortgagors keep cultivating it, the mortgagors retain occupancy rights.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser does not acquire cultivatory rights in occupancy land through decree enforcement or insolvency proceedings when the transfer is barred or lacks required revenue-authority permission.
material_facts: The mortgagees purchased one share of the land rights in execution of a civil decree based on an arbitration award and another share in insolvency proceedings.
The rights were cultivatory rights held by occupancy tenants or, alternatively, by ex-proprietary occupancy tenants.
There was no suggestion that the transfers of ex-proprietary occupancy rights had the permission of the appropriate revenue authority.
issues.conclusion: The transfers did not vest the cultivatory rights in the mortgagees, and the respondent, as the surviving holder of those rights, was entitled to restoration of possession; the appellants could not claim possession on the basis of the transfers.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act barred transfer of an occupancy tenant’s cultivatory rights in execution of a civil-court decree or in insolvency proceedings. Under section 49, an ex-proprietary occupancy tenant’s rights could not be transferred to the mortgagees in these circumstances; section 50 permitted certain transfers only with the appropriate revenue authority’s permission. The court also held that the cultivatory rights did not vest in the Insolvency Court under the Provincial Insolvency Act. It relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: possession_claim_based_on_purchased_tenancy_rights and transfer_through_decree_or_insolvency and (ordinary_occupancy_tenancy or (ex_proprietary_occupancy_tenancy and not revenue_authority_permission))

predicates.possession_claim_based_on_purchased_tena: A party seeks possession in a suit based on rights it says it purchased from a tenant.
predicates.transfer_through_decree_or_insolvency: The claimed purchase occurred through enforcement of a civil decree or through insolvency proceedings.
predicates.ordinary_occupancy_tenancy: The rights transferred were cultivatory rights held by an occupancy tenant who was not an ex-proprietary occupancy tenant.
predicates.ex_proprietary_occupancy_tenancy: The rights transferred were cultivatory rights held by an ex-proprietary occupancy tenant.
predicates.revenue_authority_permission: The transfer of the ex-proprietary occupancy rights had the permission of the appropriate revenue authority.

issues.definition: A purchaser who claims tenancy rights through decree enforcement or insolvency proceedings acquires no cultivatory rights if the rights belonged to an ordinary occupancy tenant, or if they belonged to an ex-proprietary occupancy tenant and the required permission was absent.

issues.legal_issue: A revenue authority may grant restoration of possession to a sole tenant who was dispossessed even if the application was made under a procedure directed to co-tenants.
material_facts: The respondent was dispossessed from the land and applied to the Revenue Court for restoration of her occupancy rights under sections 12 and 13 of the Act.
The court considered that she might have been the sole tenant and that section 13 relief might have been framed for a co-tenant claiming after dispossession.
issues.conclusion: The application could be treated as one under section 100 of the Act, so the grant of restoration relief was not without jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Although section 13 relief was challenged as confined to a co-tenant who had been dispossessed, a sole tenant could seek relief from the same revenue authority under section 100 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act. The application could therefore be treated as one under section 100. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.tenant_dispossessed: A tenant was dispossessed from the land.
predicates.restoration_application_to_revenue_autho: The tenant applied to the revenue authority for restoration of possession.
predicates.applicant_is_sole_tenant: The applicant was the sole tenant entitled to the tenancy rights at issue.
predicates.application_invokes_cotenancy_restoratio: The applicant sought restoration through a procedure associated with a co-tenant’s claim after dispossession.

issues.definition: When a dispossessed sole tenant applies to the revenue authority through a co-tenancy restoration procedure, the authority has jurisdiction to grant restoration.
